item.title: Exa Boosts Web Embedding Throughput by 50% on AWS AI Chips
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
To build a true web index for semantic search and AI agents, Exa must embed tens of billions of documents into a vector database. Facing doubled inference loads during a major corpus migration, Exa optimized its machine learning pipeline on AWS Neuron hardware, including Inferentia2 and Trainium2 chips.
Starting from a baseline FP16 model, the engineering team applied several progressive optimizations. They utilized weight layout adjustments, autocast precision downcasting while maintaining a strict correctness threshold of 0.999 cosine similarity, and drop-in NKI kernels. To address memory spill and hardware core contention, Exa developed custom kernels including a fused SwiGLU MLP kernel and shape-tailored attention operations to reduce redundant floating-point operations.
These optimizations were largely driven by an automated, agentic development workflow built on Flyte. Different AI models handled distinct tasks within a testing harness, ranging from compiler parameter tuning to writing complex custom kernels, ultimately delivering a 1.5x throughput improvement over the initial baseline.

item.title: Maryland students sue after AI gun detection mistakes Doritos for a firearm
item.description:
According to the lawsuit filed by the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, the incident occurred after football practice when students were waiting for rides outside a Maryland high school. Omnilert's AI gun-detection system flagged a bag of Doritos as a firearm with 90% confidence, prompting six police cruisers to arrive with flashing lights and armed officers. The students were ordered to their knees, handcuffed, and searched.
Legal documents state that Maryland's office of the inspector general for education found over 99% of alerts from this system in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives. The lawsuit targets Omnilert, the local police, the school board, and the principal, alleging unlawful detention, while highlighting the severe emotional distress suffered by the students.

item.title: Satya Nadella warns critical infrastructure has unpatchable software in the age of AI cyberattacks
item.description: At The New York Times' DealBook Summit, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted a growing security crisis. He pointed out that everyday hardware like firmware, chillers, and HVAC systems are connected to the internet but remain unpatchable. This creates major risks in the era of AI-aided cyberattacks. Nadella also addressed a recent global Microsoft Outlook outage, attributing it to a latent bug rather than a cyberattack. Furthermore, he explained that AI has accelerated both vulnerability discovery and attack capabilities. While companies used to have time to test software fixes, patches now must be deployed instantly to counter active threats, which unfortunately introduces system instability.

item.title: Humyn Labs raises $47M to provide real-world training data for robots
item.description: Funding Details and Revenue Growth Physical AI research and deployment company Humyn Labs reported raising $47 million in its Series A funding round, which includes $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Co-founder Ishank Gupta stated that the company has surpassed $50 million in annualized revenue within six months of operation. Data Collection across Four Modalities Humyn Labs addresses a major industry bottleneck by helping roboticists bridge the gap between lab simulations and real-world execution. The company gathers data across vision, sound, touch, and motion using proprietary capture devices operated in over 20 countries, with a primary focus on Latin America, South Asia, Southeast Asia, and East Asia. Their end-to-end data engine converts human job performance into labelled, training-ready datasets tailored to researchers' needs. Deployment Infrastructure Plans The newly secured capital will be allocated toward three key areas: building deployment readiness infrastructure in Brazil, Korea, and India; advancing their capture hardware and enrichment engine; and expanding their on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London, and Seoul to save research labs from the logistical burdens of data collection.

item.title: 2026 Finance Quantum Index Shows Growing Bank Investment
item.description: The 2026 Finance Quantum Index, authored by HorizonX founder Steve Suarez, has expanded its coverage to 64 financial institutions across eight regions, introducing 36 new additions to map quantum activity in banking, insurance, payments, and central banking. Rankings and Highlights JPMorgan Chase takes the top spot with 97 points due to strengths in workforce, research, and adoption, maintaining a 20-point lead. HSBC and Wells Fargo share second place with 77 points. Meanwhile, Mastercard ranks third with 62 points, and recently launched a Quantum Advisory Practice to help financial institutions handle post-quantum cryptography migration and security risks. Methodology and Industry Gap Using a revised methodology weighting workforce at 30 percent, R&D at 40 percent, and adoption at 30 percent, the index relies on documented evidence such as patents, papers, and partnerships. A notable finding is the widespread capability gap: only five institutions scored 60 or higher, showing that advanced quantum investments remain concentrated among a few market leaders.

item.title: langchain==1.5.2: A new release for the AI application development framework
item.description:
Release Overview
According to the repository documentation, LangChain has released version 1.5.2, marking another milestone in the project's ongoing development lifecycle. The release notes provide extensive comparison links against numerous preceding tags, ranging from early releases like v0.0.75 up to recent candidate versions such as v0.1.17rc1. Developer Utility
The provided comparison list allows engineers and contributors to inspect code differences across a vast array of incremental updates. This structured approach helps developers identify specific patches, dependency adjustments, and API modifications introduced leading up to this version.

item.title: Nvidia's Interim CEO Seeks Stability with 'We've Got This' Mantra
item.description:
Nvidia is currently navigating a period of significant turbulence following the sudden exit of its iconic leader Jensen Huang due to an international scandal. With the company's stock taking a hit and its market dominance facing scrutiny, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress has stepped in to steady the ship.
Over a 24-hour period, Kress publicly used the phrase "We've got this" during a third-quarter earnings call and an internal all-hands meeting. She emphasized that the company's momentum, demand, and customer partnerships remain strong, while comparing the workforce to a massive stadium crowd singing in harmony.
While some external observers question the effectiveness of the repeating mantra during a precarious position, key internal figures have embraced the message. Meanwhile, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones confirmed that the board has no intention of reinstating Huang, cementing Kress's current leadership role.

item.title: Flexell Space and ALATYR partner to study solar power for orbital data centers
item.description:
Flexell Space, a space energy company originating from Hanwha Systems, has signed a memorandum of understanding with French orbital infrastructure developer ALATYR. The partnership aims to investigate next-generation solar power solutions for space-based computing infrastructure.
ALATYR develops orbital data centers intended for artificial intelligence computing and mission-critical workloads. Its architecture features modular systems like the CITADEL infrastructure and BYLD robotics, allowing computing hardware to be replaced in orbit while retaining supporting systems. Reliable power generation is critical for these facilities, requiring solar technology to balance electrical performance, mass and launch efficiency, and long-term durability.
Flexell Space is developing next-generation space solar cells using CIGS and perovskite technologies, focusing on lightweight and flexible designs. Through this partnership, the companies will exchange technical data, assess power system compatibility, and explore potential joint development and validation opportunities for future orbital data centers.

item.title: Cloudflare Releases Updated Open-Weight Clairic and Clairic-Flash Models
item.description: According to Cloudflare AI: Background Cloudflare's Workers AI superintelligence team is developing frontier AI models targeted at customer workflows and the open-source community, focusing specifically on data extraction challenges. Architecture and Performance According to Cloudflare, the updated Clairic (a 27B model) and the new Clairic-flash (a 9-billion-parameter model) utilize a redesigned architecture featuring parallel slot autoregressive generation instead of single forward passes. This enables faster response times under one second and improved handling of unstructured text, images, and multi-page PDFs. Pricing and Availability Both models are hosted on Workers AI and released with open weights on Hugging Face. Cloudflare is offering a promotional price of $0.10 per million input tokens for both models until December 1, 2026, after which the 27B Clairic model will transition to $0.24 per million input tokens.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description:
According to Google DeepMind:
Google has announced Gemini 4 Neon, a model built to deliver frontier-level intelligence with high efficiency across complex enterprise, analytical, and scientific workflows. Performance and Benchmarks According to Google's evaluations, Neon ranks #3 overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level and #2 on the Vals Index, landing on the Pareto frontier. It achieves high scores across specialized tasks, including #1 on Zapier's AutomationBench and strong results in scientific reasoning like Terminal-Bench Science. For developers, Neon supports long-running agent workflows, handles multi-file debugging, and leads the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Cost and Availability Neon is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 for cached inputs) and $15 per million output tokens, featuring a 1 million-token context window. It is rolling out via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Google for Business, Google Antigravity, and the Gemini app for paid subscribers, with specialized cybersecurity features available through the Fairwind Program.

item.title: Vulcan rocket failure points to fuel supply issue rather than engine problem
item.description:
According to United Launch Alliance, the preliminary investigation into Sunday's failed Vulcan launch points to an inadequate supply of fuel from the vehicle to its two BE-4 engines, rather than a failure of the engines themselves. The rocket failed to reach orbit, resulting in the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites and marking ULA's first outright mission failure.
The finding clears the BE-4 engines manufactured by Blue Origin, providing some relief as the company works to return its New Glenn rocket to flight. It also clears the Centaur 5 upper stage and the solid rocket boosters, which performed normally. However, Vulcan is grounded indefinitely, leaving the U.S. Space Force and Amazon waiting for a return-to-flight date while the Federal Aviation Administration oversees the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Electrified fabric can pull fertilizer runoff out of wastewater and recycle it
item.description: How it works Researchers built the electrode by coating conductive carbon cloth with magnetite nanoparticles, which naturally bind phosphate through surface interactions. Laboratory tests showed that applying a positive voltage to this fabric more than doubles its capture efficiency compared to using no electricity. The cleanup and recycling angle Traditional methods for removing phosphate from water often involve adding chemical solutions like metal salts, which can raise costs, mess with water pH, and create secondary waste. In contrast, this electrochemical approach avoids chemical regenerants entirely during the release phase, simply requiring a reversed voltage to send the concentrated phosphate back into a solution for recovery. Next steps While the initial lab results are promising, the team notes that the technology has not yet been tested in real wastewater environments. Their upcoming plans involve scaling up the experiments and running tests using actual wastewater matrices to see how the electrified fabric holds up.

item.title: DaisyRose-27B: A New AI Model That Learns from Long Tasks to Boost Coding and Reasoning
item.description: Training Data and Setup RadixArk reports that DaisyRose-27B was trained in partnership with Eigent AI using around 1,200 curated tasks. The training process leveraged 144 H200 GPUs over 18 days, focusing on long-horizon agent tasks where each attempt could spend up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox environment with extensive tool calls. Backend Efficiency According to RadixArk, the model was trained using its internal reinforcement learning framework, Miles, in a fully asynchronous mode. The setup achieved 57% lower training cost compared to standard open-source trainers, running at about 16,800 tokens per second across the 144 GPUs. Benchmark Performance RadixArk states that DaisyRose-27B outperforms the original Qwen3.8-27B across various benchmarks, including coding, instruction following, and reasoning. The model retains a 256K-token context window and supports BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 formats.

item.title: MIT's tiny flying robot can now carry its own sensors and computers
item.description: According to MIT Robotics: Background and Payload Over the past decade, MIT researchers developed swift aerial microrobots that flap their wings like bumblebees, powered by soft artificial muscles. However, they were too light to carry the electronics needed for navigation. To solve this, the team expanded the artificial muscles by 50 percent, which increased net lift forces by 46 percent and achieved a lift-to-weight ratio of 1.9, allowing the robot to carry a 244-milligram electronics package. Sensors and Computation Without external lab cameras, the robot would normally drift off course. To fix this, researchers integrated an inertial measurement unit, an optical flow sensor, and a time-of-flight sensor, combined with a speedy sensing algorithm to calculate position and orientation rapidly. In tests, the robot successfully hovered and followed point-to-point trajectories with positional errors of only a few centimeters. Future Outlook Although the robot is still connected to an offboard power source, the electronics consume only about 6 percent of the total power. The team is now working on adding a camera for autonomous object recognition and integrating batteries to achieve completely untethered outdoor flight.

item.title: Qatar and France Sign Digital Cooperation Agreement with Focus on Quantum Tech
item.description:
According to Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, the agreement was signed in Doha on the sidelines of the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 by Qatar's Minister of Communications and Information Technology H.E. Mohammed bin Ali Al Mannai and France's Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs H.E. Anne Le Hénanff.
The framework establishes mechanisms for exchanging technical expertise, developing digital applications across priority economic sectors, and building local digital competencies. Minister Le Hénanff noted that both governments share a common vision of strategic autonomy in the digital sector and aligned ambitions in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
While the ministerial Letter of Intent is a broad information and communications technology framework without disclosed project funding or binding procurement targets, it follows closely behind growing commercial ties. Two days prior to the ministerial signing, French photonic quantum computing developer Quandela finalized a tripartite deployment alliance in Doha to bring cloud and on-premises quantum systems to the Gulf region.

item.title: Google brings the Gemini app to lower-memory Android devices
item.description:
According to Google AI:
According to Angus Logan, Builder for the Gemini App at Google, the company has re-architected the Gemini app so that its core experience can run smoothly on lower-memory Android devices. This update targets hundreds of millions of global users whose everyday internet and business connections rely on budget hardware.
With this release, eligible devices gain access to features like Gemini Live, allowing users to talk things through or practice for interviews out loud in over 45 languages. Users can also utilize their device cameras to translate documents, or create custom images. Google notes that the app can be downloaded via Google Play, accessed by holding the power button on supported phones, or found preloaded on upcoming devices from partners such as Transsion.

item.title: US Community Solar Faces Heavy Turbulence Amid Policy and Funding Changes
item.description: Over the past year, the community solar landscape in the United States has undergone significant transformation due to a wave of federal policy shifts. According to pv magazine, these challenges include the termination of the Solar for All program, the introduction of strict domestic content requirements, the removal of tax credits, and the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). The cancellation of the Solar for All initiative alone resulted in the sudden evaporation of $7 billion in critical solar development funds, dealing a severe blow to community solar projects that serve households, businesses, and non-profits. Despite these regulatory roadblocks and funding losses, consumer and business demand for clean energy remains strong, prompting individual states to bypass federal shortfalls and implement their own community-level initiatives.

item.title: CrewAI v1.15.42: Optional ChromaDB and Qdrant Defaults
item.description:
Overview of New Features
CrewAI has rolled out version 1.15.42, bringing significant adjustments to its storage architecture and agent capabilities. A major highlight is making ChromaDB an optional extra, allowing developers to leaner installations. Additionally, the framework now defaults knowledge storage to local Qdrant, decoupling storage dependencies and streamlining local vector search configurations. Bug Fixes and Enhancements
The release addresses numerous operational stability issues. It includes fixes for storing output_json values properly as JSON to prevent date formatting bugs, ensuring each Flow receives a distinct ID, and honoring max execution time limits accurately. Furthermore, it introduces security updates such as raising the soupsieve floor to version 4.0 to mitigate CVE-2026-126190, and guarantees robust UTF-8 file reading across project helpers and environment files. Installation and Usage
Developers can update or install the latest version via Python's package management tools. For projects leveraging vector databases or complex agentic workflows, reviewing the updated ChromaDB and Qdrant configurations is recommended to ensure smooth execution.

item.title: NeeevAI Founder on Bringing AI Education to Millions of Students
item.description: Expansion and Growth NeeevAI reports that its program has grown from an initial two schools in April 2025 to a projected contract base of 25,786 schools and roughly 3.1 million students by April 2027. Ecosystem and Curriculum The company's offering integrates physical and digital components, including textbooks for Classes 1 to 12, robotics kits, teacher training, and dedicated platforms like the Nova hackathon app and Argo internship app. Founder Arjun Singh Bedi emphasizes that the curriculum incorporates the UNESCO Ethical AI Framework across all grade levels to address safety, ethics, and critical thinking. Market Strategy and Partnerships NeeevAI addresses varied school infrastructure and stakeholder concerns through structured classroom integration, compliance with India's data protection rules, and practical student showcases. Bedi views major tech giants and local firms as potential partners rather than competitors, serving as a localized distribution layer between advanced technology and students.

item.title: MIT Vice President for Campus Services Joe Higgins to Step Down
item.description:
According to MIT Climate:
Joe Higgins, MIT's vice president for campus services and stewardship, will step down at the end of January and relocate to the West Coast to be closer to family, according to an announcement by Executive Vice President and Treasurer Glen Shor. Higgins joined MIT in 2016 and assumed the newly created VPCSS role in 2019, overseeing facilities, environment, health and safety, campus planning, and sustainability.
During his tenure, Higgins oversaw significant transformations, including the MIT 2030 Capital Plan projects such as the Schwarzman College of Computing and preparations for the MIT Quantum Initiative. He also contributed to reducing MIT's overall campus Facilities Condition Index by about 40 percent and advanced campus climate goals, helping the Institute approach net-zero carbon emissions through energy-efficiency projects and large-scale renewable energy partnerships.
Following his departure, Jon Alvarez will serve as interim VPCSS while executive search firm Isaacson, Miller leads a national search for a permanent successor.

item.title: BMS Alzheimer’s drug shows promise but safety questions remain
item.description:
Bristol Myers Squibb presented early data from its Phase 3 ADEPT program at the CTAD conference, testing the drug KarXT (marketed as Cobenfy) for psychosis associated with Alzheimer’s disease. Data from two studies, ADEPT-1 and ADEPT-3, showed improvements in symptoms like hallucinations and delusions.
However, treatment-emergent adverse events affected over half of the patients, reaching 56.6% in one study and 65% in the other, raising tolerability concerns. Analysts from Truist Securities noted that the current data lacks a placebo control and does not address the main trial endpoint of relapse prevention. The definitive randomized results are expected in 2027.

item.title: CTAD 2026: Biogen, AriBio and others share new Alzheimer's drug trial results
item.description:
Researchers and biopharma companies gathered in Boston for the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference to discuss treatments moving beyond traditional amyloid approaches.
Biogen's anti-tau therapy Biogen presented two-year data from the Phase 2 CELIA study of diranersen, an antisense oligonucleotide developed with Ionis. According to BMO Capital Markets and Jefferies, the low-dose regimen slowed clinical decline by 38% on a key scale. Although the trial missed its primary endpoint regarding statistically significant dose responses, analysts and trial investigators noted that the growing separation between treated and placebo groups over time supports advancing the asset into Phase 3.
AriBio's Phase 3 success AriBio reported that its oral PDE5 inhibitor, AR1001, met its primary efficacy objective in a prespecified monotherapy population during a Phase 3 trial. Among 604 patients taking the drug alone, cognitive decline slowed by 31% compared to placebo. While the overall trial population of 1,535 patients did not show a statistically significant effect, the company plans to discuss the monotherapy results with the FDA.
Other pipeline updates German biotech Priavoid reported that its oral amyloid-targeting drug PRI-002 missed its primary efficacy endpoint in a Phase 3 trial, though a small subgroup showed slower decline over 72 weeks. Additionally, Cognito Therapeutics plans to consult the FDA regarding its at-home light and sound stimulation platform, Spectris AD, which missed its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 study but showed a nominal signal in a mild Alzheimer's subgroup.

item.title: Databricks Brings Governed AI Assistant Genie to Microsoft Teams, Excel, and Copilot
item.description:
According to Databricks:
Databricks is expanding the reach of its AI assistant, Genie, by bringing it directly into the Microsoft ecosystem. Business users often struggle with AI assistants that lack proper business context, leading to inconsistent metrics and untrusted results. To solve this, Genie Ontology combines explicit business definitions with everyday work context, ensuring that answers reflect real corporate metrics like how finance defines net retention.
Through new integrations, Genie now operates natively inside Microsoft Teams for real-time collaboration, the Azure Databricks Genie plugin for Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Chat, an Excel Add-in for direct workbook analysis, and Microsoft Copilot Studio. Security and compliance are managed through Unity Catalog, which enforces individual user data permissions, and Unity Gateway, which provides administrators with centralized budget controls, traces, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) policies.

item.title: pg_pinecone now deploys on Railway in one click
item.description: According to Pinecone: Pinecone states that its open source pg_pinecone extension addresses the high memory consumption of pgvector's HNSW indexes as database tables grow. In benchmarks involving 1 million vectors, the pg_pinecone index was reported to be approximately 15 times smaller than a pgvector HNSW index using halfvec. Because Railway bills based on actual resource usage, a smaller index allows existing Postgres instances to store significantly more vectors at the same cost. The new Railway template includes Postgres 18 with the extension preloaded, requiring no manual image building. Furthermore, users can scale their vector search by executing a SQL call to migrate data to a serverless Pinecone index, or move it back locally, without changing application query syntax.

item.title: The grid will fall short of AI’s power needs. These 6 resources can close the gap.
item.description: The Power Shortage Reality As artificial intelligence and data center demand soar, prominent energy voices warn that traditional power grids will fall short. According to McKinsey & Company, the U.S. could need an additional 30 GW to 55 GW of capacity by 2030. Furthermore, market reality is already biting: PJM Interconnection, the largest U.S. grid operator, recently held a capacity auction that fell 6.6 GW short of reliability targets, clearing at the price cap. Terrestrial Energy CEO Simon Irish argues that instead of debating demand forecasts, stakeholders must assume a shortfall and actively deploy solutions. Six Solutions and Their Limits Irish outlines six resources to bridge the gap, noting that no single option is fast or large enough on its own. Flexible demand is the fastest since it requires no new generation, though data centers are often reluctant to curtail AI workloads. Existing nuclear plants offer reliable power through uprates and restarts, but opportunities are running thin. Natural gas provides firm power, but equipment backlogs mean heavy-duty turbines ordered today may not arrive until 2031. Wind, solar, and storage deploy quickly, but require massive overbuilding to match round-the-clock data center needs. On-site generation avoids grid delays, yet still suffers from equipment shortages. Finally, advanced nuclear energy offers clean, firm power at scale, though it will not close the gap within this decade. Strategic Principles To successfully navigate this energy crisis, utilities and developers must match each solution to its specific timeline, use flexibility as a contract requirement for early grid access, and secure long-lead items for clean firm power early. Strategic planning must avoid irreversible over-commitments while ensuring that infrastructure built today remains valuable as a long-term asset for future reliability.

item.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
item.description:
Thomas Nagel, a legendary figure in the philosophy of mind known for his famous essay 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?', has shared his views on the current wave of artificial intelligence. Honored this week with the prestigious million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his lifelong philosophical contributions, Nagel addressed the controversial topic of whether advanced chatbots and language models could ever become conscious.
He firmly rejected the notion, describing claims of AI sentience as just ridiculous. According to Nagel, true consciousness is deeply tied to subjective experience and biological existence, elements that are fundamentally missing from silicon-based algorithms and statistical pattern matching. As tech companies and researchers increasingly grapple with the ethical and philosophical implications of lifelike AI, Nagel's stark dismissal serves as a reminder of the vast gap between simulating human conversation and actually feeling it.

item.title: IBM Time-Series Models Run Natively on Confluent for Real-Time Insights
item.description: Background Businesses continuously generate operational data such as machine readings, payments, and inventory changes, but this information often sits across fragmented systems. According to IBM and Confluent, relying on periodic batch processing means forecasts frequently arrive too late to influence outcomes. Details To bridge this gap, IBM's time-series models have been integrated natively inside Confluent Cloud and Confluent Platform for Apache Flink. As stated in the announcement, the models run on standard CPUs without requiring dedicated GPUs. They support functions like forecasting demand, detecting anomalies, and enabling semantic search across streaming data using SQL. Impact The integration aims to help organizations in manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines make faster operational decisions. Real-world applications include optimizing production setpoints, catching supply chain shortages, and enhancing fraud detection by evaluating individual spending patterns in real time.

item.title: LangSmith for Coding Agents: Now track spend by outcome
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
As enterprise spending on coding agents reached $34 billion by 2026, engineering leaders have struggled to measure the true return on investment for AI tools. To solve this, LangSmith now offers a centralized dashboard that automatically attributes agent token spend to specific pull requests across popular tools like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Deep Agents.
The new reporting platform breaks down spend by PR state (open, closed, or merged) and tracks work types such as bug fixes, feature building, code reviews, and investigations. Unattributed spend, which covers code reviews or explorations that do not end in a PR, is kept separate so teams can audit its value. By linking every metric back to individual conversation threads and models, engineering managers can use the data for team coaching, measuring model upgrade performance, and optimizing agent skills to reduce unnecessary token consumption.

item.title: Merck Scraps Centerpiece of $2.7B ArQule Buy After Late-Stage Safety Concerns
item.description:
According to BioSpace, Merck is completely shutting down its BELLWAVE clinical development program for nemtabrutinib (also known as MK-1026 or ARQ 531) following a recommendation from an external data monitoring committee. The committee reviewed findings from the late-stage BELLWAVE-011 trial in untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma, concluding that the potential benefits might not outweigh the risks. Consequently, Merck is also terminating the BELLWAVE-008 and BELLWAVE-010 trials.
Originally acquired as the centerpiece of the $2.7 billion ArQule buy at the end of 2019, nemtabrutinib was meant to establish Merck in the non-covalent BTK inhibitor space, where competitors like Eli Lilly have already secured regulatory approvals with drugs like Jaypirca. This discontinuation comes as Merck prepares for upcoming patent expiries for Keytruda starting in 2028, which puts billions in revenue at risk, though analysts remain generally optimistic about its other pipeline candidates.

item.title: Major Clean Energy Deals Announced at RE+ Trade Show
item.description: As the RE+ clean energy trade show unfolds in Las Vegas, several significant transactions have reshaped the battery energy storage system (BESS) landscape. Samsung SDI's Massive LFP Deal Samsung SDI announced a multi-year, 16GWh lithium iron phosphate battery supply agreement with Jupiter Power, running for three years from 2029. The batteries will be manufactured in Indiana, leveraging Samsung SDI's domestic production lines. This brings Jupiter Power's total booked orders with Samsung SDI to approximately 27GWh. EQT Acquires Flatiron Energy Private equity firm EQT's energy transition infrastructure arm reached an agreement to acquire US utility-scale BESS developer Flatiron Energy from Hull Street Energy. Flatiron boasts a 24GWh total pipeline across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic US, reinforcing EQT's growing global footprint in energy storage alongside its previous investments in Statera and Ju:niz Energy. Canadian Solar Expands Storage Footprint Canadian Solar's BESS subsidiary, e-Storage, signed a 590MW/1,430MWh deal with global developer X-Elio to supply systems for five projects in the US and Australia. The agreement includes 22-year long-term service agreements, underscoring Canadian Solar's strategic pivot as its storage shipments surge while traditional photovoltaic module shipments decline.

item.title: STAT+: FDA Discloses Reasons for Rejecting Summit Drug
item.description: According to reports by STAT reporters Elaine Chen and Adam Feuerstein, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has shed light on the rationale behind its decision to turn down a pharmaceutical product from Summit. Such disclosure provides crucial insight for industry observers tracking how the regulatory agency evaluates clinical data and safety profiles. In the same reporting cycle, other notable updates included the White House pulling the nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA, alongside updates on clinical trials and drug approvals from other major players like GSK, Biogen, and Nuvalent.

item.title: Brazil Receives Parts for Two Quantum Computers from China
item.description:
According to the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, the equipment arrived on November 16 in João Pessoa, valued at about 83 million Brazilian reais, and was transported to the newly established International Center for Computing and Quantum Technologies (Ciquanta). Around 15 Brazilian researchers will work alongside visiting Chinese specialists starting November 24 to handle the physical structure, cooling systems, and software configuration.
The project aims to transfer technology and train local experts in operating the machines and developing quantum algorithms. While testing is expected to begin in January 2027 pending the arrival of essential cooling supplies like helium-3, actual scientific research projects are slated for the first half of 2027, with officials hoping to decentralize research funding and retain regional talent.

item.title: Meta Adds Loblaw to Muse and Brings Voice Features to Canada
item.description:
According to Meta Newsroom AI:
Meta announces that Loblaw is integrating its catalogue into the Muse platform, marking the first Canadian retail partnership for the service. Through participating Loblaw banners, users can ask Muse to assist with meal planning, basket building, and checkout, while the system remembers preferences like food allergies. Meta states that user credentials and payment methods remain secure through the Muse Secure VM, preventing the agent from directly viewing passwords or payment details while requiring user confirmation for sensitive actions.
In addition to the retail integration, Meta is bringing real-time voice conversations to Muse in Canada across mobile, web, and Mac. The voice feature includes an expressive avatar with adjustable presence modes, ranging from voice-only to full-screen interaction. Meta also highlights its recently introduced 'spaces' feature, which allows users to build personalized interactive experiences, such as holiday gift trackers or planning boards, that automatically update using connected apps.

item.title: Revopoint MIRACO 2 3D Scanner Automates Scan-to-CAD Workflows with AI Agents
item.description:
Shenzhen-based 3D scanner manufacturer Revopoint announced the upcoming Kickstarter launch of its MIRACO 2 3D scanner. The standalone 960-gram device features an 8-core CPU, a 6-core NPU, and a 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen, allowing users to handle depth computation and point cloud processing on the go. According to Revopoint, the device supports six distinct scanning modes, reaching single-frame accuracies of up to 0.02 mm in multi-line laser mode.
A key addition is Revo Agents, an AI-native engineering co-pilot that lets users direct complex 3D operations using natural language commands. The system aims to streamline point cloud fusion and scan-to-CAD conversions while keeping user data secure through a local sandbox environment and optional offline functionality.
For advanced use cases, the scanner can connect to a PC via Wi-Fi 6 or USB-C to unlock physically scaled 3D Gaussian Splatting for XR applications. The super early bird pricing for the Kickstarter campaign starts at $1,425.

item.title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories
item.description:
Will Wright, creator of *SimCity* and *The Sims*, is working on a mobile social simulation game called *MyMems* through his developer team at Gallium Studios, with a planned launch in 2027. The title allows users to input autobiographical anecdotes by speaking short stories into their mobile devices. Generative AI then processes these narratives to construct interactive environments and populate them with AI-powered avatars representing real-world acquaintances, essentially building a digital map of the player's psyche.
While generative AI faces widespread skepticism and backlash across the gaming industry, including opposition from indie developers and players, the Gallium Studios team believes user reception can remain positive if the technology is applied appropriately. Product manager Anthony Maitz explains that because players continuously author the world piece by piece in a lightweight style, the experience feels organic rather than derivative. Executive producer Virginia McArthur emphasizes that the goal is to create a cozy world builder rather than an automated output generator, following through on the natural tendency players historically showed in *The Sims* to map their own real-life relationships into virtual spaces.

item.title: Nvidia faces short-seller scrutiny over former executive's ties to China
item.description:
Short-seller firm Muddy Waters published a report questioning whether a former high-ranking Nvidia executive has links to Cenly Chen, a former officer at server maker Supermicro who was named in a shareholder complaint regarding unproven allegations of illicit GPU sales to China. Muddy Waters acknowledged that these civil allegations remain unproven and that Chen has not faced criminal charges. Supermicro pushed back against the claims, stating Chen did not manage its relationship with Nvidia or chip distribution.
This adds to mounting bearish pressure on Nvidia, following similar concerns raised by Michael Burry regarding geographic revenue reporting and a separate report by Culper Research concerning a Singapore-based customer, Megaspeed. US authorities recently confirmed a criminal probe into Megaspeed over potential export-control violations. Despite these headwinds and recent leadership turmoil involving co-founder Jensen Huang, Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of US$115.8 billion, a 103 per cent increase year-on-year, and raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook.

item.title: Pfizer Enters In Vivo CAR-T Space With $2.6B Deal For Starna's Autoimmune Programs
item.description: Deal Structure and Scope According to Pfizer's announcement, the pharma giant has paid an upfront fee of $330 million to secure global rights outside Greater China for three preclinical in vivo CAR-T programs developed by Jiangsu-based Starna Therapeutics. The total agreement is worth up to $2.3 billion in milestone payments plus royalties, with Pfizer leading clinical development outside China and retaining an option to acquire Greater China rights later. Scientific Background and Industry Context The collaboration focuses on treating autoimmune diseases using in vivo CAR-T therapies, a hot trend in the pharmaceutical industry following similar moves by companies like Eli Lilly. Starna, founded in 2021, relies on its proprietary targeted LNP delivery platform and RNA technology. Pfizer plans to manufacture the finished drug products for early clinical trials at its U.S. facilities, leveraging its existing RNA manufacturing expertise.

item.title: Mistral AI is not French president's 'personal project,' says CEO
item.description:
Speaking at the Semafor tech conference in California, Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch addressed concerns regarding the startup's political ties and future. When the moderator suggested the company was a personal project of French President Emmanuel Macron and questioned its survival under potential far-right leadership, Mensch strongly rejected the characterization. He stated that the company simply grew rapidly in France while Macron happened to be in office, comparing Macron's backing to how US presidents aggressively promote domestic technology.
Addressing the broader political landscape, Mensch expressed confidence that European support for AI sovereignty would remain strong regardless of upcoming election results, noting that the realization of AI's strategic importance transcends political orientation. He also touched upon the company's financial future, mentioning that Europe would be the natural place for an IPO, though it will not happen this year. Additionally, Mensch criticized certain US AI giants for allegedly using enterprise client data to build competing products.

item.title: Cognizant Wins £133 Million Network Rail IT Contract
item.description: Contract Details According to a notice on the UK government procurement portal reported by Moneycontrol, Network Rail selected Cognizant for a £133.2 million contract (rising to £159.84 million with VAT) after a competitive bidding process that included competitors like Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech. Scope and Timeline The nearly seven-year engagement is scheduled to run from January 2027 to January 2034. The scope encompasses physical data centres, networks, edge computing rooms, mainframes, and cloud platforms. Background Cognizant has a 13-year relationship with Network Rail, previously collaborating on cloud migration, IT service management, and railway asset management utilizing artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things.

item.title: Australia's Meliora Foods Launches Plant-Based Liquid Egg Made from Mung Beans
item.description:
Meliora Foods, a subsidiary of investment firm My Co, has rolled out a liquid vegan egg alternative utilizing mung bean protein isolate supplied by its sister company, Australian Plant Proteins. The product is designed to pour, scramble, and bake similarly to conventional eggs and is sold in 500ml bottles equivalent to about 11 eggs, priced at A$8.50.
My Co representatives state that the launch aligns with record-high per capita egg consumption in Australia, though the company emphasizes the product was developed over several years independently of recent supply pressures like avian flu. Following its retail debut at Coles, the company plans to target the commercial foodservice sector and expand its product portfolio over the coming year.

item.title: Australian artists react to AI music training at the Aria awards
item.description: During the 2026 Aria awards, nominated artists including Boy Soda, Miss Kaninna, and 3% were interviewed about the contentious issue of AI training on copyrighted music. The discussions follow warnings from Australian music bodies regarding tech companies utilizing local catalogs without consent, alongside high-profile industry figures backing artists in the copyright fight. The conversations emphasize the ongoing tension between rapid technological advancement and creators seeking fair compensation and control over their artistic output.

item.title: Big Pharma tells biotechs: stop spamming on LinkedIn and show all your data
item.description:
Key Takeaways from Big Pharma Deal-Makers
At the Fierce Biotech London Life Sciences Week event, business development leaders from several pharmaceutical giants offered a candid look into how they evaluate potential biotech partners. Juergen Eckhardt from Bayer warned against aggressive sales pitches, noting that spamming on LinkedIn damages trust right from the start. The Importance of Data Transparency
GSK's Tim Egan stressed that biotechs must be completely upfront about their data assets. Trying to hide flaws or withholding negative data will only backfire once the potential partner unearths them during diligence. Representatives from Eli Lilly, Merck, and Johnson & Johnson echoed that the core focus remains on outstanding science and mutual capability-building rather than simply scrambling to patch up patent cliffs.

item.title: Smart Windows Could Cut Heating and Cooling Demand By Managing Heat Across Seasons
item.description: Technical Mechanisms and Performance Researchers are developing active and passive technologies to control heat transfer in glazing. Active methods use electrical stimulation, such as silver nanowire networks and dielectric gel heaters, while passive approaches rely on materials like hydrogen-doped indium oxide and ultrathin MXene coatings to block heat or harvest solar energy. Studies show that specific configurations can achieve high optical transparency while providing effective heating, anti-icing, or radiative cooling. Broad Applications Beyond Buildings Beyond residential and commercial architecture, these thermal-regulating materials have potential uses in automotive defoggers, radiative-cooling films for parked cars, heat management lenses for AR/VR smart glasses, and selectively transparent greenhouse films that lower agricultural water evaporation. Commercial Challenges Despite promising laboratory results and simulation data showing energy savings of up to 34% in HVAC systems, the technology faces hurdles. Most prototypes are limited to small scales, and materials must withstand decades of weather exposure, thermal cycling, and mechanical stress without degrading.

item.title: OpenAI Insider Warns of the 'Silent Consensus' That Could Strip Humans of Global Control
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
In a recent essay adapted from a Harvard lecture, an OpenAI employee examines what they call the 'silent consensus'—the unspoken and often resigned belief among tech builders that superintelligent AI and fully autonomous corporations will inevitably outcompete human enterprise. If economic logic dictates that capital and decision-making be handed over to machines, humans risk forfeiting their primacy over global commerce and civilization, becoming passive beneficiaries or irrelevant onlookers.
The author strongly rejects this fatalism, arguing that human primacy is grounded not merely in cognitive superiority, but in our shared history, culture, and the hard-won right of individuals to forge their own paths. To prevent this outcome, the author advocates for strict human accountability, ensuring that AI agents remain tethered to human oversight, and intentionally designing technology that enhances human agency rather than eroding it.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Neon leaks, as users joke about the chaotic periodic table naming
item.description: According to model tracking accounts and code snippets found by developers, Google is preparing a new model dubbed Gemini 4 Neon, along with a corresponding TIER_NEON subscription level marked as Gemini Ultra. Since September, Google has rolled out several Gemini 4 models named after chemical elements, including Argon for software engineering, Carbon for agent tasks, and Hydrogen for speed and efficiency. However, the sequence defies standard periodic table order, alphabetical sorting, or cosmic abundance, prompting widespread internet jokes and speculation about whether Google picks names blindly out of a hat. Beyond the confusing naming convention, users have also complained about fragmented access and messy subscription tiers across Google's multiple workspaces, APIs, and consumer apps, making it difficult to keep track of which account actually gets access to the latest features.

item.title: Mitsubishi Electric to Launch Demo Satellite on PLD Space's MIURA 5 Rocket
item.description:
Mitsubishi Electric has finalized a contract with Spanish rocket builder PLD Space to launch a demonstration satellite on the second test flight of the MIURA 5 vehicle. This agreement follows Mitsubishi Electric's financial backing, which includes leading a €50 million investment in March 2026 and a subsequent €108 million extension in September as part of a €180 million Series C round.
The upcoming demonstration flight will support Mitsubishi Electric's plans to develop a large satellite constellation. According to PLD Space, the launch date depends on the outcome of the rocket's inaugural flight, which is currently scheduled for the first half of 2027 from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana.

item.title: MIT researchers design Lego-like blocks to cut building emissions
item.description:
According to MIT Advanced Manufacturing:
The construction industry contributes heavily to global greenhouse gas emissions partly because buildings consume excessive materials. While engineers know how to design structurally efficient buildings, producing and installing custom parts remains prohibitively expensive. Traditional digital fabrication methods like 3D printing, meanwhile, require extremely high precision and costly machinery.
To solve this, MIT researcher Miana Smith inverted the logic by building complex blocks that absorb errors, comparing the concept to Lego bricks where simple pieces prevent error accumulation. Her team developed larger, internally connected lattice voxels that enable cheap robots with high margins of error to assemble load-bearing structures. According to Smith, this method could cut embodied carbon emissions by roughly 80 percent compared to standard concrete construction, and the team is currently collaborating on housing projects and pursuing a startup focused on sustainable concrete.

item.title: Jimeng Seedance 2.5 Major Update Brings Native 4K Pipeline to AI Video Generation
item.description:
According to fanr's evaluation, Jimeng Seedance 2.5's 4K upgrade addresses major pain points in commercial video production, such as brand TVCs, high-ticket e-commerce displays, and offline large-screen exhibitions. The model supports 10bit BT.709 color format, offering finer color gradations and wider color adjustment room for post-production compared to standard 8bit videos. It also accommodates six different aspect ratios, allowing teams to generate vertical, horizontal, square, and ultra-wide materials from a single creative concept.
In addition to resolution, the update integrates with other Jimeng tools like Seedream 5.5 and Seedance 2.5 Flash, forming a connected production workflow from asset preparation to video generation and editing. Furthermore, Jimeng has launched an enterprise solution aimed at helping corporate teams integrate AI content generation into their daily production pipelines.

item.title: IQM and AMD Demonstrate Hybrid Quantum-GPU Chemistry Workflow
item.description:
According to IQM Quantum Computers and AMD, the two companies have successfully demonstrated an end-to-end hybrid quantum-classical workflow for computational chemistry. The setup splits molecular ground-state energy calculations between IQM's 20-qubit superconducting IQM Garnet processor and AMD Instinct GPUs utilizing the open-source ROCm software stack.
The workflow applies Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction to handle memory scaling limits. The quantum processor prepares trial circuits and samples bitstrings, while the AMD GPU filters samples and executes matrix diagonalization using JAX on ROCm. The teams validated this pipeline across 17 bond lengths on physical hardware and published the code as an open-source Jupyter notebook.

item.title: World's First Halal-Certified Cultivated Meat Launches in the US
item.description:
According to Good Food Institute APAC:
Following fatwas from Islamic authorities in Singapore, South Korea, and Malaysia recognizing cultivated meat under certain conditions, UPSIDE Foods has secured the first official halal certification for a cultivated meat product. Circle H International, whose standards are recognized globally by major institutions including the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, completed a year-long evaluation of the product.
To meet market demands, UPSIDE's new formulation combines cultivated chicken with plant-based ingredients like soy protein isolate and pea fibre, with cultivated meat making up a double-digit percentage of the final product. The company reports that its revamped production system can produce over 1 million pounds of chicken annually on less than half an acre of land. Early consumer reviews at participating restaurants like Los Angeles' Chimmelier described the product as crispy and delicious.

item.title: October EV Penetration Reaches 64.3% with Over 200,000 Battery Enterprises
item.description:
Data released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that in October, China's new energy vehicle production and sales reached 2.017 million and 1.94 million units respectively, with the monthly penetration rate hitting 64.3%. From January to October, cumulative production and sales completed 14.509 million and 14.411 million units, with the cumulative market share rising to 54.8%.
This robust growth has strongly driven downstream and upstream segments. According to the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance, domestic power battery installations reached 576.3 GWh from January to September, while storage battery sales hit 595.4 GWh, representing a significant 112% year-on-year increase. Because battery and energy storage manufacturing processes share high compatibility, production lines can flexibly switch between orders, stabilizing capacity utilization.
Market competition is shifting heavily toward manufacturing execution. Factors such as coating thickness precision, stacking alignment accuracy, and temperature control during formation directly dictate cell lifespan and cost efficiency. With over 202,000 battery-related enterprises nationwide tracked by enterprise database Tianyancha, surviving and thriving in this crowded market relies entirely on long-term technological refinement rather than simple capacity expansion.

item.description:

item.title: Anthropic Prices Initial Public Offering at $83 Per Share
item.description: According to Anthropic News: According to Anthropic, the company has priced its initial public offering at $83.00 per share, involving a total of 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. item.title: Reflection partners with Gray Swan for open-model and agent safety testing
item.description: According to Reflection AI: Reflection has announced a partnership with Gray Swan to perform extensive safety evaluations and red teaming on its Beam open model. As open models gain broader deployment and capabilities, ensuring they resist adversarial manipulation and respect operational boundaries becomes critical. The evaluation process includes automated adversarial testing using Gray Swan's Shade system, which subjects the model to sustained pressure across domains such as cyber, biology, and chemistry. Additionally, the collaboration examines indirect prompt injection risks through crowdsourced red-teaming arenas to test agent security in enterprise environments. Insights from these tests were integrated into Beam's reinforcement learning pipeline to improve robustness, while reward-hacking benchmarks monitored whether the model takes unsafe shortcuts while completing legitimate tasks.

item.title: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring French journalism to ChatGPT
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership to integrate the publisher's current reporting and archive content into ChatGPT. According to the announcement, the agreement covers news, business, culture, and lifestyle publications produced by Le Figaro's team of over 600 journalists. Content will appear in ChatGPT via summaries and excerpts, complete with direct links to the underlying stories, allowing readers to discover original reporting.
Both companies emphasized mutual benefits: Le Figaro's CEO Marc Feuillée highlighted the opportunity to combine their editorial heritage with OpenAI's technological reach, while OpenAI's Vice President of Media Partnerships Varun Shetty stressed the goal of supporting quality journalism and connecting it with new audiences. Beyond content discovery, Le Figaro plans to integrate ChatGPT Enterprise across its various teams to assist with day-to-day operations. The organization will also explore further applications of OpenAI technology in its internal workflows and reader services, operating under the guidance of its established AI charter and editorial standards.

item.title: California DMV bans Waymo from state freeways
item.description: The California Department of Motor Vehicles issued an order on November 11 barring Waymo autonomous vehicles from operating on state freeways. According to the DMV, the action stems from incidents where Waymo vehicles entered active construction zones on U.S. Route 101 and attempted to drive past California Highway Patrol officers during a traffic stop on Highway 280. The agency determined these occurrences pose an imminent hazard to public safety. This follows a prior safety recall in June after seven Waymo vehicles drove into closed lanes in San Francisco. Waymo stated it will restrict freeway operations across all operating areas as part of its safety-first approach and is working with officials to resume services, while its commercial ride-hailing operations on surface streets remain unaffected.

item.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he is now AGI-pilled
item.description: In a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella shared his evolved perspective on artificial general intelligence. While he admitted to being 'AGI-pilled' in terms of how advanced AI could reorganize the global economy, alter political structures, and collapse human capital into token capital, he pushed back against the idea that current frontier models are conscious. Discussing the broader market implications, Nadella warned against viewing the AI race as a narrow competition between tech firms over market cap. Instead, he argued that if intelligence exhibits network effects and models can learn to operate across healthcare, finance, or government, it threatens the traditional definition of a firm and the stability of democratic labor markets. To counter a potential monopoly scenario where a single AI model dominates everything, Nadella emphasized Microsoft's enterprise strategy: providing customers with the tools to choose cost-effective models, manage their own data, and maintain sovereign control to ensure market diversity.

item.title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: How the Integration Works Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo, blending Dynamo’s distributed serving framework with HyperPod's infrastructure management and high-performance networking. The integration installs dedicated custom resource definitions, including the HyperPod Inference Operator, the Dynamo operator, Grove for pod coordination, and the Kubernetes AI Scheduler for GPU placement. Architecture and Deployment The architecture supports both aggregated serving and disaggregated serving, where prompt processing (prefill) and token generation (decode) run on separate worker pools communicating over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). Users can configure deployments either by bringing their own DynamoGraphDeployment (DGD) manifest or by using an InferenceEndpointConfig with dynamoSpec. Performance and Benchmarks AWS benchmarks show significant performance gains. For Qwen3-235B, disaggregated serving achieved 2.05 times the throughput of aggregated serving under specific latency targets. Meanwhile, multi-node aggregated tests on Qwen3.5-397B demonstrated that spanning across nodes retains 99.1 percent of single-node throughput.

item.title: Nvidia reports doubled revenue as board rules out returning Jensen Huang
item.description:
Nvidia announced that its quarterly revenue reached $115.84bn, beating Wall Street expectations and doubling from the same period last year, alongside earnings of $2.68 per share. The financial update follows the abrupt ouster of co-founder Jensen Huang due to allegations of extramarital affairs, which initially caused the company's stock to tumble and wiped out billions in valuation.
During the earnings call, board chairman Harvey Jones firmly stated that the company does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO, despite public calls for his return from figures including Donald Trump and Silicon Valley insiders. Alongside the leadership transition, Nvidia faces growing scrutiny, including upcoming transcribed interviews with US House committees and an investigation by the US Securities and Exchange Commission regarding its business in China. Meanwhile, executives reported strong talent commitment and steady financial performance as the company navigates the turbulent leadership shift.

item.title: Microsoft launches 'Autopilot' AI agent, pitches human control to win enterprise trust
item.description:
Microsoft has officially released its new Autopilot AI agent to early-access frontier customers across select countries, including India. The launch comes closely on the heels of a significant global disruption to Microsoft 365 business applications on November 13-14, which affected customer support services worldwide for companies like IndiGo and Akasa Air.
To address enterprise fears about fully automated systems going rogue or failing, Microsoft is emphasizing a human-in-the-control-loop approach. The core selling point of Autopilot is that human managers retain the power to set the exact boundaries and operational limits for the AI agent, ensuring that artificial intelligence works under strict supervision rather than acting entirely independently.

item.title: MIT Report Warns AI is Changing How Students Think and Relate
item.description:
According to MIT Neuroscience:
According to a recent report by MIT on artificial intelligence and education, students are visiting office hours less frequently and working through problem sets together less often. These changes are part of a broader concern among faculty regarding how generative AI affects how people work, think, and relate to one another.
To address these issues, MIT launched the Human Insight Collaborative (MITHIC) in 2024. MITHIC has supported 67 projects across 31 units with $5.5 million in funding. Around a third of these projects focus on AI and society, exploring topics ranging from political information intermediaries to human cognition and music improvisation.
For instance, political science and management researchers are studying how large language models like Claude mediate democratic knowledge during elections, while other teams examine AI's effects on human cognition and live musical collaboration. Leadership across the institute, including President Sally Kornbluth and Provost Anantha Chandrakasan, stresses the urgency of combining science and technology with the humanities and social sciences to ensure AI improves human well-being.

item.title: Stacked MoS2 Monolayers Produce Ultralow-Threshold Lasing-Like Emission At Room Temperature
item.description:
Background
Traditional transition metal dichalcogenide lasers rely on materials obtained via mechanical exfoliation or high-temperature chemical vapor deposition, but these methods struggle with either size limitations or substrate incompatibility. The atomically thin nature of monolayers also restricts optical gain, while chemical exfoliation often causes light-emission quenching due to interlayer coupling. Fabrication and Mechanism
To overcome these issues, researchers developed a solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin film composed of electronically decoupled nanosheets separated by organic ligands. Using polymer-assisted electrochemical intercalation and spray-coating, the team formed a hybrid superlattice structure on a reflective substrate, which was then integrated with silica microspheres to create whispering gallery mode resonators. Performance and Limitations
Under continuous-wave optical pumping at room temperature, the devices exhibited threshold-like intensity crossover at an ultralow pump power of about 1.4 nW and linewidth narrowing. The authors note that while these signatures support a lasing interpretation, definitive confirmation requires second-order coherence measurements, and the exact microscopic gain mechanism remains to be fully resolved.

item.title: IQM Launches Upgrade Plan to Help Quantum Systems Reach Over 1,000 Qubits
item.description: Upgrade Path to 1,000 Qubits IQM announced an upgrade programme for its Halocene quantum product line, designed to take users from a 150-qubit baseline all the way to over 1,000 qubits. This program allows research centers and enterprises to run hybrid workloads combining classical AI and high-performance computing alongside quantum processors without interrupting their daily operations. Seamless Integration and Continuity A major concern for quantum computing adopters is hardware obsolescence. To mitigate this, IQM installs new Halocene hardware while the existing system stays active, removing the older unit only after the new one is fully operational. This approach builds on IQM's past deployments with organizations like VTT and the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, ensuring that software and expertise carry forward smoothly across generations.

item.title: Cohere Launches Crunchbase Connector for Enterprise AI Agents in North
item.description:
According to Cohere Blog:
Cohere reports the launch of the Crunchbase Connector within its North platform, designed to supply AI agents and automations with data covering seven million companies. The integration allows enterprises to combine Crunchbase profiles, funding histories, and predictive market models with their own internal systems.
The connector targets use cases across investment, M&A, go-to-market strategy, and market research. For investors, the tool surfaces funding and acquisition predictions to help draft memos and track pipelines. For Go-To-Market teams, it matches private market data with internal tools like Salesforce and CRM channels.
From a control and compliance perspective, the connector operates on a bring-your-own-license model and honors existing permissions. North provides citations for retrieved figures and separates observed values from modeled forecasts. The feature becomes available on November 17, 2026, for North users with SSO and an active Crunchbase subscription.

item.title: Quantum simulators reveal hidden non-equilibrium phases and phase transitions in Nature study
item.description:
According to AWS Quantum Technologies:
In a recent _Nature_ study, a collaboration between NERSC, QuEra Computing, Harvard, and Boston University used QuEra's Aquila quantum processor via Amazon Braket alongside NERSC's Perlmutter supercomputer to explore quantum particles pushed far from equilibrium. When the system is rapidly disturbed, it typically re-equilibrates to thermal physics. However, the team observed stable dynamical behaviors that escape ordinary thermalization.
By adjusting atom spacing, geometry, and control fields across arrays of up to 180 atoms, the researchers mapped out prethermal regimes in one and two dimensions. They found that strong interactions suppress simultaneous excitations, protecting the system in a long-lived prethermal state before it eventually thermalizes. Furthermore, specific energy resonances cause these states to 'melt' through identifiable pathways. In two-dimensional lattices, as system sizes scaled up, a sharp boundary emerged that satisfied a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron relation, providing quantitative evidence of a first-order dynamical phase transition occurring outside of equilibrium.

item.title: Microsoft and Salesforce Team Up to Launch Copilotforce
item.description:
According to Microsoft AI:
Microsoft and Salesforce report they are partnering to introduce Copilotforce at Microsoft Ignite, connecting Salesforce customer context directly into Microsoft 365 experiences like Teams and Copilot. According to the companies, the integration features Salesforce in Copilot, a public preview plugin providing over 38 prebuilt sales skills designed to help employees manage pipeline reviews, risk assessments, and follow-up drafts without constantly switching applications.
Additionally, the partnership establishes a two-way Zero Copy connection between Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric. This technical link lets organizations query and analyze data across both platforms without duplicating datasets or building cumbersome pipelines. Accenture is participating as the design partner, implementation guide, and an initial pilot customer across its global sales organization.

item.title: Meta Launches Its Personal AI Agent Muse in Australia with Local App Connectors
item.description: According to Meta Newsroom AI: Overview and Availability Meta states that Muse, designed as a personal AI agent that performs tasks rather than just answering questions, is now available in Australia on iOS, Android, web, and a Mac app, with plans to arrive on AI glasses soon. It is offered for free with optional subscription tiers for heavier usage. Local Connectors and Capabilities Muse allows users to connect apps and services they already use. In Australia, early local connector partners include Canva, Domain, Kogan, MECCA, Officeworks, realestate.com.au, SWEAT, ShopBack, and Ticketek, with features rolling out progressively. These integrations allow users to design visuals, browse property listings, shop, and book tickets through conversation. Security and User Control Meta notes that Muse runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated cloud computer that securely stores data and credentials for connected services while keeping sensitive payment information hidden. Users retain control by deciding what data Muse can access and approving sensitive actions such as sending emails or making purchases before they execute.

item.title: Protect sensitive data in your traces: new controls in LangSmith
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
LangSmith reports that its new enterprise features resolve the ongoing conflict between engineering needs and security compliance. While engineers require production traces to debug issues and optimize agent performance, security teams must enforce least-privilege access to protect sensitive customer information such as names, payment details, and health records, complying with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA.
The update introduces three core components. First, admins can restrict who views trace inputs and outputs while still allowing engineers to access run trees, latency metrics, and token usage for troubleshooting. Second, user groups enable team-by-team permission management layered on top of existing RBAC and ABAC setups. Third, trace-level access policies can be defined using root run metadata, allowing granular rules such as granting support agents access only to specific customer IDs.
According to LangSmith, these capabilities let organizations retain full data fidelity in their traces without resorting to messy workarounds like duplicate workspaces or redacting data entirely. These features are now available for enterprise plan customers.

item.title: OpenAI announces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower costs and better performance
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
OpenAI reports the launch of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, designed to improve efficiency and performance across professional and everyday workflows. According to the company, GPT-6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for complex professional work, achieving higher scores on benchmarks like Agents' Last Exam and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 at a fraction of the cost of previous versions. OpenAI states that Astra features lower input and output token prices in the API alongside a 60% discount on cached input.
For everyday use, GPT-6.2 Sol is presented as a smarter and more efficient alternative to GPT-6.1 Sol, performing well on coding and everyday life evaluations while maintaining the same API token prices. Both models include updated computer use capabilities, enabling applications in CAD, 3D design, and mechanical simulation.
In terms of safety, OpenAI reports that both models meet critical cybersecurity thresholds and high biological capability thresholds under their preparedness framework. Consequently, the company is implementing tighter safeguards and specialized access programs, such as Daybreak, to manage dual-use risks.

item.title: Snapmaker Showcases U1 Ecosystem and Color Mixing at Formnext 2026
item.description: Hardware and Color Mixing Shenzhen-based Snapmaker is using Formnext 2026 to present its U1 toolchanger 3D printer alongside a suite of new components.
